title: Acceptance specs assert on implementation internals and exact output strings, not outcomes
evidence: tests/soccer.test.ts:57 asserts m.homeKey==='palmeiras' (internal field); tests/soccer.test.ts:77 toMatch(/1\. Flamengo - 90 pts \(28W, 6D, 4L.*Champion/) pins the exact formatted string. Per _atdd_review.md Priority 1 (lessons 103b/203), ~half the sample-question specs are 'narrowly correct' and would break under a reimplementation.
suggestion: Assert domain outcomes (champion=Flamengo, points=90) via a DSL rather than regex over formatted output or internal keys.

title: Wall-clock performance assertion in the correctness suite is an intermittency risk
evidence: tests/soccer.test.ts:169 expect(performance.now() - t).toBeLessThan(2000) inside the pass/fail suite. _atdd_review.md Priority 3 (lesson 306) flags resource contention as a named flakiness cause; under CI/parallel load this can fail with no regression.
suggestion: Move the timing check into a separate performance budget that does not gate releasability.

title: No DSL layer between specs and SUT (effectively two layers)
evidence: tests/soccer.test.ts:11 const ask=(tool,args)=>runTool(svc,tool,args) is a stringly-typed pass-through at SUT API level; other specs call svc.* directly. _atdd_review.md Priority 2 (lessons 305/301): no domain vocabulary, defaults, or insulation layer.
suggestion: Introduce a thin domain DSL (e.g. soccer.headToHead(...), soccer.leagueTable({season})) over runTool.

title: Specs pin exact counts from vendored Kaggle CSVs (data-drift coupling)
evidence: tests/soccer.test.ts:39-41 toBe(10296)/toBe(18207) and :76 points:90 depend on the exact external dataset loaded once in beforeAll (:10). _atdd_review.md Priority 3 (lessons 306/302): refreshing the CSVs turns green tests red without a regression.
suggestion: Give standings/coverage specs small synthetic fixtures they own, instead of asserting on the full real dataset.

title: Weak threshold assertions hedge against data drift
evidence: tests/soccer.test.ts:56 toBeGreaterThan(30), :61 toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(10), :100 toBeGreaterThan(20). _atdd_review.md section 4: these are hedges; with owned fixtures the exact outcome could be asserted.
suggestion: Once specs own their data, assert exact expected values.
